facts.name: says we are not on pace

answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
**Yes on pace to date — we're at 103.3% of the goal to date — but no on the Election Day goal: if nothing changes we land at 57,329 doors, 3,303 short of the 60,632 goal (94.6%).**

- To date (Sep 21 to Oct 18): 33,503 doors against a goal to date of 32,431, or 103.3% of pace [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Projection method: 33,503 doors + 1,489.1 average daily doors over the last 7 days × 16 knocking days left (Oct 19 to Nov 3) = 57,329, which is 94.6% of goal, a shortfall of 3,303 doors [table:v_office_pace_total] [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]
- Northside is the only office projected to clear its goal: 23,583 projected vs 22,675 goal (+908, 104%), with pace to date 112.5% [table:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate is the big drag: 14,596 projected vs 17,800 goal (−3,204, 82%), pace to date only 89.3% [table:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 19,150 projected vs 20,157 goal (−1,007, 95%), pace to date 105.3% [table:v_office_pace]
- Program-wide it would take 33.3 shifts per day, 4.1 more per day than the 29.3 we're running, to pull back onto goal [table:v_office_pace_total]

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
**Ask the client for more doors first — the pace we've shown would run out of untouched first-pass turf well before Election Day, so a second pass is only the fallback.**

- Capacity left for the rest of the program: **23,826 doors** (1,489.1 average daily doors last 7 days × 16 knocking days left, Oct 19 to Nov 3) [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Untouched doors remaining in our turf: **10,393**, out of 41,853 turf doors [table:v_office_pace_total]
- So capacity is more than double the untouched doors left; we're already at **75.2%** of turf touched, with 31,460 doors touched once [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Program-wide we project **57,329** doors against a 60,632 goal, a shortfall of **3,303** (94.6% of goal) — the extra turf is also what closes that gap [table:v_office_pace_total]
- How the call is made: when projected capacity for the rest of the program exceeds untouched doors, ask for more doors first; a second pass on not-home doors is the fallback because it contacts voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]

A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's sheet counts every attempt pulled at the end of the day, before QC rollbacks; our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed, so Oct 12 shows 1,484 "doors" reported against 1,281 in our dashboard — a gap of 203, mostly Eastgate rollbacks.

- Oct 12, program total: client reported 1,484, our dashboard 1,281, gap 203 [table:v_client_vs_dashboard_total]
- Of that gap, 142 are rolled-back attempts (all at Eastgate) and 61 are repeat attempts at the same door [table:v_client_vs_dashboard_total]

answer.question: Which precincts are untouched or only lightly touched, and is what's left dense enough to keep knocking efficiently?
answer.answer:

cases.question: Which offices or canvassers have the most duplicate registrations, and is it one person or across the board?

answer.question: Which offices or canvassers have the most duplicate registrations, and is it one person or across the board?
answer.answer:
Across the registration drive to date, **112 of 3,781 cards were duplicates (3%)**; **Harbor has the most by office**, but the problem is heavily concentrated in **one canvasser, Renata Cole**.

- Program total: **3,781 cards collected, 112 duplicate cards, 3% duplicate rate** [table:v_vr_pace_total] [table:v_vr_pace].
- By office: **Harbor 66 duplicates of 1,312 cards (5%)**, **Northside 24 of 1,506 (1.6%)**, **Eastgate 22 of 963 (2.3%)** [table:v_vr_pace].
- Top canvasser: **Renata Cole, Harbor — 42 duplicates out of 129 cards (32.6%)** [table:v_vr_canvassers]. That is **37.5% of all 112 duplicates** and **63.6% of Harbor’s 66** [table:v_vr_canvassers].
- It is not only her: **21 of 28 canvassers have at least one duplicate**, but the next highest counts are **Emmett Delgado with 7 (1.9%)** and several canvassers with 6 (1.8%–2.3%) [table:v_vr_canvassers]. Only Cole is above the **10%** retraining threshold [table:v_vr_canvassers].
- Method: a duplicate is a second card for a registrant already in the drive; only valid cards, with duplicates removed, count toward the goal. A canvasser above 10% gets a retraining conversation [doc:registration-drive#valid-cards-and-duplicates].

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person could walk to them and knock.

- A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the flagged window stop counting as doors or contacts [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data with rolled_back = true, but are removed from doors and contacts [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]

cases.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?

answer.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?
answer.answer:
Payroll runs Tuesday at noon for the week that ended Sunday, and overtime needs the field director's approval.

- Payroll timeline: every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; anything still pending or marked needs_fix after that rolls to the next payroll [doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]
- Approval: every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM for the week that ended Sunday, which pays out Tuesday at noon [doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]
- Overtime threshold: over 40 paid hours in a payroll week (Monday to Sunday), counting every shift the person worked; hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
- Overtime sign-off: any shift that takes a person over 40 hours needs the field director's approval and stays pending until approved [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
- Shifts marked needs_fix (for example a missing clock out) can't be paid until a field lead corrects the record [doc:payroll-rules#shifts-that-need-fixing]

cases.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?

answer.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?
answer.answer:
Record the building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit, then move on — don't mark every unit.

- Apartments: each unit is its own door and must be knocked individually [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Locked building: record it once, as "inaccessible", on the first unit only [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Don't mark the whole building from the lobby — that would be householding, a QC flag [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]

sources.text: When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

FROM v_weekly_hours h

I can't confirm that from the program data or documents. There is no data on canvasser attrition, notice, or intention to leave, and no document with a method for predicting who will quit before Election Day.

What the data does show is only current and past status, not future plans:
- Staff type and activity are counted by the plan's definitions: regular = 5+ days worked, one-day hire = exactly one day, active = worked a shift in the last 7 days [doc:program-plan#staff-definitions]
- The closest available figures are counts per office in `v_gotv_staff` (active canvassers, active regulars, active occasional, active one-day hires) and per-person days worked, first shift and last shift in `v_canvasser_status` — these describe who has been working, not who will stop.
- Missing: any retention, turnover, scheduling-commitment or resignation information.

sources.text: When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

facts.name: Harbor GOTV cost per door, Oct 12 to 18

answer.question: What's Harbor's GOTV cost per door for this week alone?
answer.answer:
Harbor's GOTV cost per door for this week (Oct 12 to 18) is $1.71.

- GOTV wages this week: $5,821.76 [table:v_weekly_shifts]
- Doors this week: 3,412 [table:v_weekly_pace]
- Cost per door: $5,821.76 / 3,412 = $1.71 [table:v_weekly_shifts]
- For comparison, Harbor's cost per door to date is $1.78 ($20,182.92 over 11,351 doors) [table:v_cost_per_door]
- Method: GOTV wages (paid hours × the person's hourly rate) divided by doors for the same office and period, with overtime premiums left out [doc:payroll-rules#cost-per-door]

The existing cost-per-door view is to date only, so this week's figure is calculated from this week's wages and doors.

sources.text: When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

Every Monday we send the client one table for the week that ended Sunday, one row per office plus a total: doors, contacts, registration cards, and paid hours. Doors and contacts use our dashboard definitions (doors once per day, rollbacks removed). Cards are valid registration cards, duplicates removed. Hours are paid hours for GOTV and registration shifts together; shifts still missing a clock out are left out and noted.

sources.text: A door is one address unit (a house, or one apartment unit) knocked on one day. Our dashboard counts each door once per day no matter how many times it was knocked that day. answer.question: Which registration canvasser has collected the most valid cards, and what share of their QC calls came back confirmed?
answer.answer:
Emmett Delgado of Northside has collected the most valid cards, **367**, and **70.1%** of his QC calls came back confirmed.

- Valid cards: **367** (374 collected minus 7 duplicates) [table:v_vr_canvassers]
- QC calls: **101 confirmed out of 144**, or **70.1%**; 32 unreachable and 11 wrong information [table:v_vr_canvassers]

cases.question: Program-wide, was our GOTV cost per door higher this week or last week? Give both.

answer.question: Program-wide, was our GOTV cost per door higher this week or last week? Give both.
answer.answer:
Program-wide GOTV cost per door was slightly **lower this week ($1.79) than last week ($1.80)** — last week was the higher of the two.

- This week (Oct 12 to 18): $18,614.16 in GOTV wages ÷ 10,424 doors = **$1.79 per door** [table:v_weekly_shifts_total]
- Last week (Oct 5 to 11): $15,923.92 in GOTV wages ÷ 8,863 doors = **$1.80 per door** [table:v_weekly_shifts_total]
- So the program spent a cent less per door this week despite knocking 1,561 more doors (10,424 vs 8,863) [table:v_weekly_pace_total]
- Cost per door is GOTV wages (paid hours times each person's own hourly rate) divided by doors for the same period, with overtime premiums left out [doc:payroll-rules#cost-per-door]
